text:
maria: heads up — noticed a latency bump on streaming requests after yesterday's release, p95 up ~100ms for short responses
cheng: saw the CI perf job failure too, streaming-throughput regressed ~18% on the microbench
ryan: any obvious suspects from the diff?
lisa: I ran a quick flamegraph on a canary and saw a spike in `kv_cache::evict_if_needed` around sequence boundaries
maria: yeah, same. The commit that landed was 191b2c — it changed the batching window + kv eviction heuristic (shrank soft-eviction window and prioritized batch packing)
aj: shrinking the eviction window to favor denser batches was supposed to reduce token cost, but could cause more cold cache churn for toolcall+stream flows
cheng: profiler link: https://perf.internal/flame/191b2c-kv-evict — you can see repeated KV load stalls when a toolcall inserts state, causing stream frames to wait for serialization
ryan: that matches what I see in trace sampling: extra 60–90ms tail per request when KV miss hits during SSE chunking
maria: sample trace (sanitized):
```
SEND CHUNK -> wait(kv_load) -> serialize(tool_result) -> flush
kv_load: 70ms median on miss, warm: 5ms
```
lisa: CI bot output posted a failing test: `streaming_latency_regression` showed p95 210ms vs baseline 110ms
ci-bot: test streaming_latency_regression: FAILED (p95=210ms, baseline=110ms, delta=+100ms, threshold=+20ms)
aj: can we toggle the heuristic remotely? I thought rollout flag `runtime.micro_batch_v2` gates the new packing behavior
maria: yes — we can flip `runtime.kv_soft_eviction_enabled=false` as a quick mitigation and hold the canary
cheng: deploy-bot: starting canary rollback toggle in prod-west at 11:05 UTC
deploy-bot: executed change: set `runtime.kv_soft_eviction_enabled=false` for tag=canary-prod-west
ryan: after toggle, preliminary canary metrics look better: p95 down to ~120ms, throughput back within 5% of baseline
lisa: we should open a bisect to the exact commit range, but commit 191b2c is highly suspicious. Also need to evaluate interaction with toolcall serialization batching
maria: I started a local bisect: testing commits 191a..191c, I'll post results in this thread shortly
aj: short-term: hold the rollout and flip flag for other regions. medium-term: rework eviction policy so we favor affinity for recent toolcall keys and avoid immediate eviction across micro-batch boundaries
cheng: can we add a perf/unit test that simulates toolcall-heavy streaming traces so CI will catch regressions earlier?
sre-bot: registered perf test `streaming_toolcall_kv_churn` in perf-suite, running nightly
ryan: also add a microbenchmark that measures kv miss latency distribution under the new packing (so we don't regress on tail)
lisa: if bisect pins 191b2c we'll revert the change and re-iterate with improved heuristics; otherwise we need a more surgical fix
maria: bisect update: 3 commits tested so far, 191b2c reproduces the regression locally. Confirming now with larger sample
cheng: cool — I'll draft the revert PR and include a follow-up that implements softer eviction + affinity map for toolcall keys
aj: PR should include the new perf test and a note about serialization ordering being sensitive to kv miss jitter
maria: thanks — for the rollout: keep current flag disabled everywhere until revert merges and passes canary. I'll update the incident channel with status
deploy-bot: canary flag set globally: `runtime.kv_soft_eviction_enabled=false`
ci-bot: perf-suite nightly job queued: streaming_toolcall_kv_churn
ryan: one more datapoint — observed increased number of small batches being flushed early due to the packing change; that interacts badly with the eviction timing
lisa: agreed. The packing change reduces batching lateness but increases KV pressure at micro boundaries. We need a hybrid approach
maria: action items: (1) aj/cheng draft revert PR, (2) cheng add perf test and sample traces to CI, (3) ops keep flag off globally until revert + canary pass, (4) follow-up design: affinity map + gentle eviction window.
aj: will do. tagging @sre for rollback if anything goes sideways
sre-bot: acknowledged. paging on-call if rollout reverts fail
maria: thanks everyone — big win that flag toggle bought us time. keep replies short and post numbers only.
